title: Session-aware sampling + per-slice privacy & latency metrics for streamed token outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
We currently emit aggregate metrics for streaming requests (total tokens, complete response latency). Customers building low-latency experiences depend on per-slice visibility (early-chunk latency, time-to-first-meaningful-token) and need assurances that logs/metrics do not leak PII when partial outputs are buffered or retried by compatibility layers.

Goal:
1) Add session-aware sampling for streamed responses to produce representative per-slice latency/throughput histograms without logging raw token payloads.
2) Attach lightweight tracing spans that represent partial-output boundaries and reassembly events so we can correlate SDK buffer behavior with backend tokenization events.
3) Introduce a configurable differential-redaction layer that replaces token payloads in telemetry with privacy-preserving fingerprints (token count buckets, token-type flags) while preserving cardinality for debugging.

Success criteria / acceptance criteria:
- Per-slice latency histograms emitted to metrics backend (percentiles for prefix, middle, suffix slices).
- Span model: create PartialOutput spans with attributes {slice_index, slice_size_tokens, reassembly_flag} and ensure span links to request-level span.
- Redaction: no raw token strings are present in any metrics, logs, or traces by default in prod; a debug-mode toggle for safe capture behind RBAC for red-team/SE support.
- SDK compatibility: older SDKs that coalesce streaming events behind a buffer will still map to PartialOutput spans via a shim so metrics can surface reassembly latency.
- Unit and integration tests covering sampling rates, edge cases with very short/very long streams, and retried chunks.

Proposed approach (high-level):
1) Sampling: implement session-aware sampler in gateway that computes a hash over request id + session id and chooses a sampling bucket. Sampling decision must be sticky for the full session to avoid fragmentary telemetry. Default sample rate: 1% sessions, with an adaptive override if error rate or latency SLO violations exceed threshold.
2) Per-slice metrics: define token-slice boundaries based on emitted stream frames (not bytes). Emit metrics: slice_latency_ms, slice_tokens, slice_idx, io_wait_ms. Use labels: model, deployment, region, sampler_bucket. Avoid including raw text as labels.
3) Tracing spans: add PartialOutput span type emitted when a frame is flushed from runtime. When SDKs do local buffering, the SDK shim will emit a Reassembly span capturing buffer_hold_ms and emitted_frame_count and link it to PartialOutput spans via span_id references in metadata headers.
4) Differential redaction: before any telemetry leaves the runtime/gateway, run a redactor that replaces token content with a token-class fingerprint (e.g., "NUMERIC_HEX", "IDENTIFIER", "COMMON_WORD") and stores only counts and fingerprint flags. Debug capture requires an enterprise RBAC flag, KMS-wrapped temporary key, and an audit log entry.
5) SDK compatibility shim: ship light binary in 4.x SDKs that adds per-frame metadata and optional Reassembly spans, and a server-side fallback where shims aren't present (heuristic mapping by timestamps).

Telemetry plan and dashboards:
- Grafana: new dashboard panel for per-slice percentile latency (p50/p95/p99) and slice drop rate.
- Traces: add trace view that groups by sampler_bucket and shows PartialOutput -> Reassembly link sequences.
- Alerts: warn when time-to-first-slice > 300ms or slice reassembly rate > 0.5% for > 5m.

Rollout strategy:
Phase 1 (canary): enable sampling=2% in staging region for internal teams only; enable redaction enforcement in prod but keep debug capture off.
Phase 2 (expanded): enable 1% sampling across all prod regions; release SDK shim as opt-in.
Phase 3 (GA): default sampler 1% with adaptive bumping; SDK shim enabled by default for supported SDK versions.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for sampler determinism and sticky behavior across reconnects.
- Integration tests with the 3.x and 4.x SDKs to validate Reassembly span linking.
- Privacy audit smoke tests to verify no raw tokens in traces/metrics under prod policies.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Sampling frequency vs. fidelity: higher sampling yields better diagnostics but increases PII exposure risk if debug capture is misconfigured. Recommend conservative defaults.
- Token fingerprint granularity: fine-grained classes help debugging but may increase re-identification risk. Work with privacy to finalize a taxonomy.
- SDK shim adoption: server-side heuristics will be lossy; we need to track adoption to know when we can turn off heuristics.

Notes / rationale:
- We prioritize sticky session sampling to provide complete sequences in traces (helpful for root-cause of transient latency spikes).
- A differential redaction approach allows us to keep actionable signals (counts, token-types) while minimizing exposure of user content.

Deliverables:
- Design doc (confluence) with privacy taxonomy finalized.
- Runtime change: sampler + per-slice metrics + redaction pass.
- SDK shim release and compatibility tests.
- Grafana panels and alerting rules.
